questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is evaluating the current statutory qualifications to enter a collaborative practice agreement. Which statements reflect M.G.L. c.112, § 24B1/2(b)? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Hold a current Massachusetts pharmacist license, currently practice in the Commonwealth, and maintain at least $1,000,000 of professional liability insurance.
Have earned a PharmD degree or completed five years of experience as a licensed pharmacist, or the equivalent.
Devote a portion of practice to the defined drug-therapy area and complete at least five additional related CE contact hours in each agreement year.
Apply for the statute's limited MassHealth ordering/referring participation if implementing regulations governing that participation are promulgated.
A pharmacist with a current PharmD must also complete five years of licensed-practice experience because the degree alternative is no longer recognized by statute.

questions.stem:

Case B: The pharmacist later obtains prescribing authority under the agreement and overlooks the separate periodic pain-management training requirement.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The CDTM framework permits its five additional hours to replace five of the general 20.
Prescribing CDTM pharmacists have a separate stated pain-management training obligation.
Pain-management training can never contribute to the additional CDTM hours.
Ending the year's CE courses permits immediate disposal of all agreement-related evidence.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is commissioning an automated system that counts tablets, fills vials and applies labels. choices.text: Comingling lot numbers in one cell is prohibited outright.
The pharmacy must hold a policy to quarantine all comingled lots if a single lot is recalled.
A pharmacist's visual check of the finished vial satisfies the verification requirement.
Controlled substance accountability need not be addressed until the system handles Schedule II drugs.

choices.text: A mandatory CDTM attestation is not converted to a recommendation by language in another prescribing pathway.
Any CPA grants retail authority to prescribe Schedule II–V drugs.
A signed CPA replaces the applicable MCSR and DEA registration requirements.

choices.text: Because methylphenidate is Schedule II, the ADD may operate without reconciliation if a perpetual inventory is kept elsewhere
Machine-specific DEA registration and Massachusetts controlled-substance registration as required for routine dispensing

Loading by a certified pharmacy technician or pharmacy intern under pharmacist supervision
Because gabapentin is Schedule VI, any unlicensed employee may load the entire machine

In a long-term care facility, the facility's medical director or designee approves.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is reviewing the range of actions the Board may take on a complaint. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts supervising physician refers a patient for collaborative drug therapy management, records the referral and the patient's consent in his own chart, and tells the collaborating pharmacist that the documentation is complete and nothing further is needed. In the pharmacist's record alone, since the pharmacist delivers the service.
In whichever of the two records the professionals agree should hold them.
In the patient's record, by the pharmacist and by the supervising physician.
In a register filed with the Board, separately from the patient's record.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is considering a nonprescription retail sale of a medicinal preparation that has already been confirmed to qualify for the controlled-substance exception described in M.G.L. c. 94C §4. Which §5 controls still apply to the sale? Select all that apply.

Diagnose asthma and begin treatment after obtaining a second patient consent, without changing the referral or agreement.
Begin asthma treatment now and have the supervising physician add asthma to the agreement retroactively by the end of the day.
Continue authorized hypertension management and return the new wheezing for physician evaluation before expanding collaborative management to that condition.
Manage the new condition without another referral because the individual-referral limitation applies only to controlled-substance therapy.
